title.narrative: Promoting Civic Space: A Public Interest Litigation Approach” – regional: Burundi, Uganda en Tanzania - Avocats sans Frontières (ASF)

description.narrative: CSOs, State Actors, Non-State Actors, Regional institutions

Contribute to a Rule of Law compliant and Human-rights based approach to Eastern Africa’s socio economic development through regional cooperation and networking between local civil societies organizations. CSOs influence decision makers and stakeholders to foster the realization of human rights and Rule of Law (i) A regional CoP allows CSOs’ coordination and peer-to-peer learning; (ii) Members of the CoP lead effective Public Interest Litigation; (iii) Collective advocacy is strengthened and effectively employed to influence decision-makers at national and regional levels

In Eastern Africa, civil society participation in the governance of public affairs is increasingly perceived as a threat by national Governments, and thus dealt with as such. The project’s foreseen impact is to contribute to a Rule of Law compliant and Human-rights based approach to Eastern Africa’s socio economic development through regional cooperation and networking between local civil societies organizations. This project (part of call for proposal is complementary to ASF’s foreseen DGD Programmes 2022 – 2026 in Uganda, Burundi and Tanzania as it develops a regional level of civil society coordination in making use of the Law for broader social change. The project articulates several of the call for proposals’ specific objectives. The project relies on the strengthening of capacities of effective, democratically functioning, accountable and sustainable local civil society organizations and the strengthening of regional cooperation and networking between local civil society organizations as a strategy to promote opportunities for open dialogue between governments and civil society. The expected impact is a shift in the paradigm that underlies socio economic development. This transformation is operated through the promotion and adoption of a Human-rights based approach (HRBA), which places the expectations and experiences of the local populations at the core of decision making (Public Interest Litigation). The outcome relocates the Rule of Law and Human Rights as the key principles guiding authorities’ actions towards development goals. The project, titled "Promoting Civic Space: A Public Interest Litigation Approach", focuses on Burundi, Uganda, and Tanzania within the sector of Government and Civil Society. Democratic Participation and Civil Society. This initiative is a response to ongoing abuses against civil society in Eastern Africa, particularly by members of the Imbonerakure, the ruling party's youth league, and local officials who enjoy near-total impunity (source: 61789_BUDG_DESC_Bijlage_5c_budget_ASF_call_civic_space_justi). These abuses are part of a larger global trend to restrict civic space, as documented by the UN Special Rapporteur on the Rights to Freedom of Peaceful Assembly and Association (source: 61787_PROGDESCR_Bijlage_5_Projectvoorstel_ASF_regionaal_opro). The reduction of civil society's participation in governance poses a threat to its democratic nature and the socio-economic development it supports in the Eastern African context (source: 61789_BUDG_DESC_Bijlage_5c_budget_ASF_call_civic_space_justi). The project aims to counter these dynamics through a Public Interest Litigation approach.
